title: Artifact provenance
description: Sits beside every raw artifact in intake/<su-slug>/<fy>/, and beside every committed derived product in derived/. Two kinds, because they answer different questions. A `sourced` record answers WHERE DID YOU GET THIS AND WHEN: raw artifacts are never edited, and this file records the URL, the retrieval and the hash. A `derived` record answers WHAT DID YOU RUN, ON WHAT INPUTS, AT WHAT VERSION -- routing output and geocoding output have no source URL, and forcing them into the sourced shape would produce a provenance record that cannot answer the only challenge anyone will make of them, which is 're-run it yourself'.

kind.description: Omitted means `sourced`, which is what every intake record is. Not defaulted by the validator: the schemas in this repo declare defaults for a human reader and ajv is configured not to fill them in, so an omitted field cannot masquerade as a deliberate one.

derivation.description: How a committed derived product was produced. Everything here exists so a reader who disputes an output can reproduce it: the algorithm and its version, the exact pinned inputs, the parameters, and the hash of what came out.

algorithm.description: Slash-separated name of the computation, e.g. `geocode/school-municipality` or `routing/nearest-same-grade-span`.

algorithm_version.description: Bumped whenever the output could change for unchanged inputs. A derived record whose version never moves is a record nobody can date.

engine.description: External engine and version where one did the work, e.g. `valhalla 3.4.0`, or the service endpoint for a hosted one.

inputs.description: Every input pinned to something immutable -- a git sha, an intake artifact plus its hash, a dated API snapshot. An input recorded as a bare path is not pinned and the output is not reproducible.

parameters.description: Settings that change the output, recorded so a rerun is a rerun and not a fresh experiment.

file.description: Filename within this directory, exactly as released. Never renamed for tidiness.

source_url.description: Where it came from. Null only when retrieval_method is 'email' or 'in_person', in which case `note` must explain.

sha256.description: Hash of the file as retrieved. CI re-verifies this on every PR; a mismatch means the artifact was edited, which is never permitted.

supersedes.description: Filename of an earlier artifact this one replaces, e.g. a revised budget book. The earlier file stays in the repo.
